project_type: Guild Wars 2 translation overlay: a DirectX 11 proxy d3d11.dll + a runtime-loaded bronco_ocr.dll (C++20, MSVC, CMake+vcpkg x64-windows-static-md), plus a standalone Python dictionary-generator tool.
build_system: C++: CMake with CMakePresets.json (preset windows-msvc) + vcpkg triplet x64-windows-static-md, built ONLY on Windows CI on tag push (~30 min per build). Python tool: no build, run directly with python3.
test_framework: No unit-test framework. Python tool has offline self-checks via `--dry-run` (run_self_checks in generate_dictionaries.py). C++ has no tests; validation is CI build + manual in-game.
build_command: C++ (CI/Windows only): cmake --preset windows-msvc && cmake --build build/windows-msvc --config Release. CANNOT build in this Linux sandbox.
test_command: Python tool: python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --dry-run  AND  python3 -m py_compile on changed .py files. C++: no runnable tests in sandbox.
verification_instructions: Python: run `python3 -m py_compile` on every changed .py file, then `python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --dry-run` (must exit 0), then a real sample generation with `--no-translate` to prove the new skills_tooltips.json + fact_labels.json are produced. C++: cannot compile in sandbox; instead perform meticulous static review (variable scope, exact types, every new method declared in the matching .h, nlohmann::json usage, balanced braces, no undeclared identifiers, no block-scoped var used outside its block). New config keys must be consistent across config.h + config.cpp (load AND save) + config/bronco_config.json.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Generated dictionaries live in data/dictionaries/pt-br/*.json and (new) data/skilldata/pt-br/skills_tooltips.json. Regenerate via the dictionary-generator tool. The tool's cache/ (raw API + translations) is gitignored and already populated with the full skills endpoint (~4800 skill objects across cache/raw/skills/en_*.json), so sample generation works OFFLINE with --no-translate.
setup_instructions: Python tool: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r tools/dictionary-generator/requirements.txt. For real EN->PT translation also run `--install-model` (Argos, ~100MB, needs network). --dry-run and --no-translate need NO network and NO argostranslate. NOTE Python 3.9 (sandbox): argostranslate install may fail (needs spacy<3.8 first); NOT needed for --dry-run / --no-translate which is all that runs in-sandbox.
environment_constraints: Network mode assumed COMMON_DEPENDENCIES/limited: do NOT rely on live GW2 API calls or Argos model download during sandbox verification. The dictionary-generator raw API cache is ALREADY populated under tools/dictionary-generator/cache/raw/skills/, so sample dataset generation runs fully offline via --no-translate. The C++ DLLs CANNOT be compiled in this Linux sandbox (Windows/MSVC/vcpkg only); CI builds on tag push (orchestrator side, ~30 min). Do NOT push or tag.
contribution_requirements: C++20, namespace bronco::, #pragma once include guards, /// doc comments on public functions. bronco_ocr.dll already depends on nlohmann/json (use nlohmann::json for parsing skills_tooltips.json). Follow existing code style. Commit to main; do NOT push/tag (orchestrator handles release).
key_patterns: 1) BroncoOcrResult marshalling: originalText/translatedText are const char* into handle->resultStorage std::strings; resultStorage MUST be reserve()'d to the hard cap BEFORE the emit loop so no reallocation dangles pointers, and emitted count is capped at BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS. The loader (ocr_loader.cpp processFrame) resizes outResults to BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS before the call. If the cap changes, both ocr_api.h #define and the loader allocation stay in sync automatically (loader uses the macro). 2) Dictionary::normalize = lowercase + collapse-whitespace + trim; skill NAME matching already works via DictionaryManager::translate (exact then fuzzy). 3) Overlay renders matched-only, de-duped, capped 8, TextWrapped; drag = Right Ctrl (isDragModifierHeld / g_captureMouse); F8 toggle. 4) Config keys are read in loadInternal AND written in save() AND present in config/bronco_config.json; getters use shared_lock. 5) Loader resolves bronco_ocr.dll relative to proxy DLL dir; data paths from config are relative to the GW2 process CWD. 6) A prior build failed C2065 from a block-scoped variable used outside its block (fixed by hoisting to function scope) - do NOT reintroduce this.
real_data_findings: From tools/dictionary-generator/cache/raw/skills/: skill objects have keys name, type, description, facts[], flags[] (only NoUnderwater, GroundTargeted observed), categories[] (Arcane, Kit, Meditation, ...). facts[] fact.type values observed in REAL data include the briefing's 18 PLUS 'BuffArray' and empty-string type, so the generator and the C++ formatter MUST handle unknown/unlisted fact types gracefully (fallback to translated label + any present value). 774 distinct fact labels exist and some contain HTML-like markup e.g. '<c=@abilitytype>Field Damage</c>' which must be stripped before translation/display. Buff/PrefixedBuff facts carry the meaningful info in 'status' (e.g. Might, Crippled, Regeneration), 'duration', 'apply_count', and 'description' (the generic 'text' is 'Apply Buff/Condition'); PrefixedBuff also has a nested 'prefix' with its own status/description. There is NO dedicated per-game-mode note field; the closest structured signals are flags[] and categories[].
directory_structure: tools/dictionary-generator/ = Python tool (gw2_api.py fetch+cache, translator.py Argos wrapper, generate_dictionaries.py CLI, cache/ populated raw API + translations). src/ = C++: proxy/ (d3d11 proxy), hook/, overlay/ (imgui_overlay), ocr/ (Tesseract engine + C API ocr_api + runtime loader ocr_loader), translation/ (dictionary + translator, compiled INTO bronco_ocr.dll per src/ocr/CMakeLists.txt), pipeline/, config/, cache/ (LRU), log/. config/bronco_config.json = default config. data/dictionaries/pt-br/ = generated dictionaries. .github/workflows/build-release.yml = CI packaging. scripts/ = install/uninstall PowerShell.
